description: Original fictional IT runbook passages written for this course. They describe no real organization, system or incident and are not operational guidance.

passages.title: Server disk nearly full
passages.text: When a server reports disk usage above 90 percent, find the largest directories with a disk usage summary, archive or delete rotated log files older than the retention period, and confirm that free space has recovered. Do not delete database files or active logs. If usage returns above 90 percent within a day, open a capacity ticket.

passages.title: User password reset
passages.text: To reset a user's password, verify the user's identity through the approved second channel before making any change. Issue a temporary password that expires at first sign-in and require multi-factor enrolment. Never send the temporary password in the same message as the username.

passages.title: VPN client cannot connect
passages.text: If the VPN client fails to connect, check that the device clock is correct, because certificate validation fails when the time is wrong. Confirm the user's account is not locked and that the client version is supported. Collect the client log before reinstalling the client.

passages.title: TLS certificate about to expire
passages.text: Renew a TLS certificate at least fourteen days before it expires. Generate a new key pair, request the certificate from the approved authority, install it on every load balancer in the pool, and verify the served certificate's expiry date from outside the network.

passages.title: User reports a phishing email
passages.text: When a user reports a suspected phishing email, ask them not to click links or open attachments. Collect the full message headers, search for other recipients of the same message, and remove copies from mailboxes. If the user entered credentials, reset their password and review recent sign-ins.

passages.title: Restore a file from backup
passages.text: To restore a file from backup, identify the last backup taken before the file was damaged or deleted. Restore it to a separate location first, compare it with the user's description, and only then replace the current copy. Record the backup identifier in the ticket.

passages.title: Sustained high CPU on an application server
passages.text: If CPU usage stays above 85 percent for more than fifteen minutes, identify the processes using the most CPU and check whether a recent deployment or scheduled job started at the same time. Scale out the service pool if demand increased; roll back the deployment if a new release caused the load.

passages.title: Print jobs stuck in the queue
passages.text: When print jobs remain stuck in the queue, check that the printer is online and has paper and toner. Cancel the oldest stuck job, restart the print spooler service on the print server, and ask the user to resend the document.

passages.title: Repeated account lockouts
passages.text: If an account locks repeatedly, look for a device or saved credential that keeps sending an old password, such as a phone mail client or a mapped drive. Unlock the account only after the source is found and updated. Many lockouts from unfamiliar addresses should be escalated to security.

passages.title: Internal names do not resolve
passages.text: When internal host names fail to resolve, test resolution against each internal DNS server directly. If only one server fails, remove it from the resolver list and restart its DNS service. Check that recent zone changes did not delete the affected records.

passages.title: Monthly patch window
passages.text: Apply operating system patches during the approved monthly window. Patch a test group first, wait one business day for problems, then patch production in batches. Keep the previous image available so a failed patch can be rolled back.

passages.title: Laptop for a new employee
passages.text: Prepare a laptop for a new employee by enrolling it in device management, installing the standard image, and enabling disk encryption before first use. Assign the device to the employee in the asset register and confirm their accounts are active on the start date.
